macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. inflation cooled to 3.4% in July
items.summary: The Labor Department said U.S. inflation eased to 3.4% in July, slightly down from the previous month. The reading adds to the recent mix of softer inflation data that markets are watching for Fed policy implications.

items.title: Retail sales fell 0.6% in July
items.summary: U.S. retail sales dropped 0.6% in July, the steepest monthly decline since May 2025. The weaker consumer-spending data is feeding debate over growth momentum and the policy outlook.

items.title: Treasury yields ease ahead of Fed minutes
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield eased toward 4.7% as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes for fresh guidance on the policy path. The move followed a recent bond-market selloff and was seen as a key driver for equities and the dollar.

items.title: Global bond selloff continues to pressure markets
items.summary: Reports described a broad bond-market selloff that pushed borrowing costs higher across major economies and helped lift mortgage rates in the U.S. The rise in yields has been a major headwind for stocks, especially rate-sensitive sectors.

items.title: U.S. stocks fell as chip shares and yields weighed on sentiment
items.summary: Wall Street's major indexes closed lower in the latest session, with the Nasdaq-100 down 1.68%, the S&P 500 down 0.69%, and the Dow down 0.22%. Semiconductor stocks led the decline as bond yields hit multi-decade highs and inflation and geopolitical concerns weighed on risk appetite.

items.title: European shares slipped on oil and bond-yield surge
items.summary: The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 0.5% as rising crude prices and higher euro-zone bond yields pressured equities. Energy shares were among the few gainers as Brent crude climbed toward $90 a barrel.

items.title: Dollar hovers near multi-month low as yields ease
items.summary: The U.S. dollar traded near multi-month lows against major peers after Treasury yields pulled back from recent highs. Traders were focused on the Federal Reserve's July minutes for clues about the next policy move.

items.title: Fed minutes were the main central-bank event in focus
items.summary: Markets were awaiting the Federal Reserve's July meeting minutes for details on the policy outlook, with yields and the dollar both reacting to the anticipation. Separate commentary also said the Fed is expected to signal a pause after its latest rate cut while it evaluates incoming data.

items.title: Trump delayed new tariffs on Canadian goods
items.summary: Reporting said the Trump administration held off briefly on new 50% tariffs for Canadian goods while trade talks continued. The move reduced some immediate trade-war pressure but kept tariff risk in focus for markets.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum edge higher while XRP and Dogecoin slip
items.summary: Bitcoin rose 0.23% to about $64,421 and Ethereum gained 0.36% to about $1,913, while XRP and Dogecoin were modestly lower in late-session trading. The broader crypto market was mixed, with traders watching macro headlines and support levels for BTC.

items.title: SEC proposes new crypto capital-raising rules
items.summary: The SEC unveiled a new framework called "Regulation Crypto Assets," aimed at giving token issuers clearer paths to raise capital and defining when crypto assets may no longer be treated as investment contracts. The proposal includes two exemptions from Securities Act registration requirements.

items.title: Treasury releases draft stablecoin regulations under GENIUS Act
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury presented draft rules to implement the GENIUS Act, the first federal law governing payment stablecoins. The draft sets out requirements for issuers, reserves, and supervision of dollar-pegged stablecoin issuance.

items.title: Blockchain Association backs SEC move to scrap outdated NMS rules
items.summary: The Blockchain Association supported the SEC's proposal to scrap outdated NMS rules, arguing that the changes could improve conditions for tokenization. The group framed the move as beneficial for modern market structure and blockchain-based assets.

items.title: Curve founder says FATF pressure could make DeFi safer
items.summary: Curve founder comments suggested that pressure from the Financial Action Task Force could ultimately make DeFi safer and more decentralized. The remarks reflect ongoing debate over whether tighter oversight strengthens or constrains decentralized finance.

items.title: Bitcoin trades around $64K after recent volatility
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $64,600 in one market update and around $62,800 in another, showing continued intraday volatility rather than a decisive trend. Analysts cited ETF flows, macro conditions, and market sentiment as key drivers.

items.title: Ripple partners with South Korea's Jeonbuk Bank
items.summary: Ripple announced a partnership with Jeonbuk Bank in South Korea focused on cross-border payments. The deal is another sign of continued enterprise payment adoption for blockchain infrastructure.

items.title: Kraken expands stock trading for EEA customers
items.summary: Kraken began offering U.S. stock trading to customers in the European Economic Area, broadening its product mix beyond crypto. The move highlights continued exchange diversification into traditional financial products.

items.title: Upbit and Bithumb report sharp first-half revenue declines
items.summary: South Korea's two largest exchanges, Upbit and Bithumb, reported 50% declines in first-half revenue. The results point to a broader contraction in trading activity and market demand.

items.title: Toyota Finance launches tokenized bond via Toyota Wallet
items.summary: Toyota Finance launched a ¥1 billion tokenized bond accessible through Toyota Wallet, adding another major corporate use case for blockchain-based financial products. The development is part of a wider push into tokenized fixed-income instruments.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI pauses frontier model training over cyber risk
items.summary: OpenAI said it temporarily halted reinforcement-learning training on its newest models after preliminary evidence suggested its upcoming Astra model could reach a critical cybersecurity threshold under its preparedness framework. The move follows broader scrutiny of autonomous AI cyberattack risks and a company overhaul of its safety procedures.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly adds teen-focused ChatGPT safeguards
items.summary: OpenAI launched or is launching a teen-oriented version of ChatGPT with parental controls, study tools, and stronger safeguards. The announcement reflects a wider industry shift toward age-specific AI products and more explicit safety controls.

items.title: Nvidia backs OpenAI's Ohio data center with major financing support
items.summary: Reports say Nvidia is guaranteeing land, power, and buildout for a large OpenAI data-center project in Ohio, underscoring how AI scaling is increasingly tied to infrastructure and capital commitments. The deal comes amid rising concern over the size of frontier-model training spend and the availability of compute.

items.title: Stripe reportedly buys OpenRouter for more than $7 billion
items.summary: Bloomberg-reported acquisition news says Stripe has finalized a deal to buy AI gateway startup OpenRouter for more than $7 billion. If confirmed, the deal would signal growing competition to control the routing layer between developers and multiple model providers.

items.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.3 with stronger coding and agent performance
items.summary: Chinese AI company Z.ai launched GLM-5.3, with reports saying it improved coding benchmarks substantially without changing the base model architecture. The release adds pressure on Western frontier labs by emphasizing cheaper, open-weight alternatives with strong developer performance.

items.title: AI safety and cyber defense move to the center of model development
items.summary: Across multiple reports, companies are responding to frontier-model security concerns by tightening monitoring, pausing training, and expanding safeguards. The trend suggests that cybersecurity, evaluation, and agent containment are becoming as important as raw model capability in the latest AI race.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA 6 gameplay and map footage reportedly leak ahead of Rockstar’s upcoming reveal
items.summary: Multiple outlets reported that apparent Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay clips and a full map image circulated online shortly before Rockstar’s planned Netflix/YouTube presentation. The leak has driven major discussion across gaming media and added urgency to the game’s next official update.

items.title: Rockstar plans a new GTA 6 extended look on Netflix, with a YouTube release to follow
items.summary: Coverage says Rockstar’s next GTA 6 video will premiere on Netflix first and then arrive on YouTube a few hours later. That unusual rollout has made the reveal one of the biggest industry talking points in the last day.

items.title: NBA 2K27 details revealed, including new gameplay features and career mode additions
items.summary: 2K shared new information about NBA 2K27, including core gameplay details and a career mode featuring Vince Staples. The announcement is one of the day’s notable sports-game updates.

items.title: Pokémon Pokopia surpasses 5 million units sold
items.summary: Nintendo and The Pokémon Company announced that Pokémon Pokopia has sold more than 5 million copies worldwide in just over four months. The milestone makes it one of the standout commercial stories in recent gaming news.

items.title: Apple revises App Store rules in the EU after pressure from regulators
items.summary: Apple announced major changes to its EU App Store fee structure, including a reduced 5% fee for external app digital transactions. The move is an important industry development for mobile gaming and app distribution.

items.title: Warren Spector retires from game development
items.summary: Warren Spector, known for Deus Ex and immersive sim design, announced that he is retiring from game development. The news marks the end of a significant career in the industry.

items.title: NVIDIA GeForce Now comes to Firefox
items.summary: NVIDIA expanded GeForce Now browser support to Firefox, letting users stream more than 5,000 PC games directly in Mozilla’s browser. It is a notable cloud-gaming platform update.

items.title: Sonic Frontiers passes 5 million copies sold
items.summary: SEGA reported that Sonic Frontiers has now sold more than 5 million copies. The milestone reflects continued momentum for one of SEGA’s biggest recent releases.
